title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition
author: Priya Nair
content:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational procedures and policy guidance across budgeting & forecasting, procurement and contracts, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business unit owners to ensure consistent controls, timely approvals, and GAAP-aligned revenue treatment for our usage-based, reserved capacity, and enterprise-licensed products.

Scope:
- Applies to all spend and revenue-related activities across Redwood Inference, including Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers: annual & rolling forecasts, capital vs. operating budgeting, procurement sourcing & PO lifecycle, contract review & signoff, and revenue recognition and invoicing for: usage (per-token/embedding), reserved capacity commitments, and professional services.

High-level responsibilities:
- Finance (FP&A): lead annual budget, manage rolling forecasts, consolidate business unit plans, financial modeling, and reporting to leadership.
- Legal: contract terms & risk assessment, approval of non-standard clauses, data residency / compliance clauses.
- Procurement: vendor management, PO issuance, contract repository, supplier onboarding.
- Sales & Customer Success: ensure contract terms match commercial commitments (billing frequency, discounts, prepaid/commit design).
- Product/Engineering: provide product pricing and feature-change inputs that affect revenue and costs.

Budgeting and forecasting cadence:
1. Annual planning (Oct–Dec):
   - Finance issues budget templates and model assumptions by Oct 15.
   - Business units return draft budgets by Nov 15.
   - Cross-functional review and leadership review in Dec.
   - Board/ExCo approval target: first week of Jan; finance publishes final budget by Jan 10.
2. Rolling monthly forecast:
   - FP&A publishes updated forecast model by the 2nd business day of each month.
   - BU owners submit updates by the 5th business day.
   - Finance finalizes consolidated forecast by the 8th business day.
3. Re-forecast triggers:
   - Material change > 10% of forecasted ARR or any supplier concentration risk > 15% of COGS.

Budget structure and controls:
- Chart of accounts mapping: all budget line items must be mapped to the canonical COA prefixes (COGS_, S&M_, R&D_, G&A_).
- Capital vs operating classification guidance with spend thresholds: 
  - Capitalizable if > $50k and useful life > 12 months and approved by CFO.
  - Operating otherwise.
- Budget change requests > $100k require Finance + CFO signoff; > $500k escalate to CEO.

KPIs and financial targets used in planning:
- Target gross margin by product line (monthly): Hosted API 68%+, Dedicated 55%+, Private deploys 48%+ (initial on-prem uplift varies).
- Target DSO: <= 45 days for invoiced customers; collections escalation at 60/90/120 days.
- Target variance tolerance vs budget: +/- 3% headcount; +/- 5% opex, material variance requires action plan.

Procurement procedures (vendor lifecycle):
- Vendor selection: competitive sourcing for > $50k TCV or 12-month contracts; sole-source requires documented justification and Procurement + Legal approval.
- Supplier onboarding: procurement collects W9/W8, insurance certificate, security questionnaire if access to systems/data.
- Purchase requisition -> PO issuance steps:
  1. Requester creates PR in procurement system with business justification and budget code.
  2. Manager approval required for PR for amounts > $5k; Finance BU owner approves budget allocation.
  3. Procurement validates vendor and issues PO.
  4. For recurring SaaS or cloud spend, a 12-month review cadence is required.
- PO thresholds and signoff matrix:
  - <= $5k: Manager approval.
  - $5k–$50k: BU Director + Procurement.
  - $50k–$250k: VP Finance + Procurement + Legal review (if contract).
  - > $250k: CFO approval + Legal and Procurement.

Contract & legal process (commercial contracts):
- Contract intake: All commercial contracts must be submitted via the Contracts intake form (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contracts-procurement-playbook-2026).
- Standard templates: Use the canonical templates for: Enterprise Subscription Agreement, Hosted Terms of Service, Professional Services SOW, MSA for Private deployments. Non-standard terms must be flagged and approved.
- Review checklist for each contract (minimum):
  - Parties & effective date
  - Commercial terms: fees, billing cadence, termination rights, renewal terms
  - Data residency & security obligations (required for Private deployments)
  - Intellectual property & license grants
  - Indemnities & liability cap (typically limited to amount paid in prior 12 months; exceptions require Legal + CFO approval)
  - Confidentiality & permitted disclosures
  - Audit & subcontracting rights
- Contract turnaround SLAs:
  - Standard template with no redlines: Legal review within 2 business days.
  - Minor redlines (commercial comments only): Legal review within 5 business days.
  - Major redlines (policy/compliance changes): 10–15 business days; notify Stakeholder with timeline.
- Signatory authority:
  - Sales Director / Head of Sales can sign SOWs <= $100k where template terms are unchanged and revenue term <= 12 months.
  - VP Sales or CFO sign Enterprise contracts <= $1M.
  - > $1M or non-standard risk: CEO + Legal signoff.

Revenue recognition and billing policy (summary):
Principles: recognition follows GAAP (ASC 606 principles where applicable) and matches performance obligations to revenue streams. Redwood recognizes revenue when control of promised goods/services is transferred to the customer and the transaction price can be reasonably measured.
Revenue streams and treatment:
- Hosted API (usage-based per-token/embedding): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (point-in-time or over time depending on contract; typically ratably during the billing period). Uninvoiced usage recorded as contract asset at period end.
- Reserved/Dedicated capacity (subscription/commit): Recognize ratably over the contractual term once the customer has the right to use capacity. Upfront prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and amortized.
- Private deployments (license + implementation + support):
  - License: determine if license is distinct; if yes and perpetual, recognize per license guidance; if term-based, ratably over term.
  - Professional services (implementation): if services are distinct and billed separately, recognize upon completion of milestone or over time if criteria for over-time revenue met.
- Credits, refunds and discounts: apply as contract modifications under ASC 606 – treat as either variable consideration with constraint or as a reduction of transaction price depending on the facts.
- Contract modifications & renewals: evaluate each change for distinct goods/services; if modification adds distinct performance, account for as separate contract. If not distinct, adjust the existing revenue schedule prospectively.

Billing and invoicing rules:
- Standard billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or quarterly in advance for subscription commitments as negotiated.
- Invoices must include: contract ID, PO number (if provided), period of service, detailed usage or subscription line items, tax line, payment terms.
- Payment terms default: Net 30 for SMB customers; Net 45 for enterprise unless a different term is negotiated and approved by Finance.
- Late payment and collections: interest at 1.5% per month after 30 days (where legally allowed); collections escalation: 30 days (CS outreach), 60 days (Legal notice), 90+ days (suspend service & collections agency).

Controls and audit readiness:
- Revenue close checklist (monthly): reconcile invoice system to general ledger, unbilled receivables to usage logs, deferred revenue rollforward, and revenue-recognition journal entries.
- Segregation of duties: Sales creates contracts but billing & revenue recognition are controlled by Finance. Procurement issues POs; requester cannot both approve and pay.
- Documentation retention: contracts and amendments stored in the contract repository for 7 years; supporting invoices and SOWs retained per records policy.
- External audit: provide sample contract-to-revenue mappings, deferred revenue rollforwards, and cut-off testing to auditors on request.

Operational SLAs and targets (examples):
- Contract review SLA (Legal): standard templates – 2 business days; minor redlines – 5 business days.
- PO issuance: Procurement to issue PO within 3 business days after approvals complete.
- Vendor onboarding: complete within 7 business days for standard vendors; 15 business days for vendors requiring security review.
- Invoice processing (AP): process supplier invoice & submit to GL within 5 business days of receipt.
- Revenue recognition close: monthly close complete and journal entries posted by 7th business day.
- DSO target: <= 45 days.

Operational play examples (step-by-step):
A. New vendor > $50k annual TCV:
  1. Requester fills PR + business justification.
  2. Procurement issues RFP or single-source justification.
  3. Finance validates budget and funding.
  4. Legal reviews contract terms; procurement negotiates commercials.
  5. PO issued; vendor onboarding performed; AP routes first invoice to finance for coding.
B. Customer contract with prepayment + usage overage:
  1. Sales enters commercial terms into CLM and tags billing model.
  2. Legal reviews and approves redlines.
  3. Finance sets up billing schedule (deferred revenue for prepayment + monthly usage tracking).
  4. Billing issues invoice for prepayment and monthly usage; revenue recognized per policy.

Escalation matrix and exceptions:
- Any contract that increases indemnity, changes liability cap, or adds data residency exceptions must be escalated to Legal Lead and CFO for approval.
- Emergency procurement (security patch, outage mitigation) can be approved by VP Engineering + Procurement but must be documented and retroactively approved by Finance within 5 business days.

Appendices:
- Appendix A: COA prefixes and budget mapping (example lines):
  - COGS_API: GPU runtime & cloud egress
  - COGS_INFRA: Dedicated cluster costs
  - S&M_SALES: Sales commissions & travel
  - R&D_ENGINEERING: Runtime engineering payroll
- Appendix B: Common contract templates (links to repository)
- Appendix C: Revenue recognition examples (journal entry snippets):
  - Prepayment $120,000 for 12-month Dedicated subscription: Dr Cash $120,000; Cr Deferred Revenue $120,000. Monthly recognition: Dr Deferred Revenue $10,000; Cr Revenue $10,000.
  - Usage invoice $5,000 invoiced in March relating to March usage: Dr AR $5,000; Cr Revenue $5,000.
